metadata.note: The Akron - Delphos line in Ohio under its four passenger operators, 1882-1951, and the Akron, Canton & Youngstown's own Akron - Mogadore line. The AC&Y never reached Canton or Youngstown. Six features, each drawn only for its report's drawable span: AC&Y Akron - Delphos 1920-1951 (last mixed train 20 Jul 1951); Lake Erie & Western (Northern Ohio Division) 1900-1919 [OPEN both ends]; Pittsburgh, Akron & Western 1891-1894 [OPEN end]; AC&Y Akron - Mogadore motor cars 1920 [ANCHOR]; Cleveland, Delphos & St. Louis narrow gauge Delphos - Columbus Grove 1882 [ANCHOR] and Columbus Grove - Mount Blanchard 1883 [ANCHOR]. The four Akron - Delphos-era features share one geometry (Rule 4 splits).
metadata.ownership_split: CD&StL (narrow gauge, 1882-1885) -> Eastern & Western Air Line 1 Nov 1885 -> Cleveland & Western 1 Aug 1886 (neither drawn: no passenger year sourced) -> Pittsburgh, Akron & Western 1890-1895 -> Northern Ohio Ry leased to the Lake Erie & Western 1 Oct 1895 -> leased to the AC&Y 1 Mar 1920. NOT splits: the PA&W receivership 1893-1895; NYC stock control of the LE&W from 1900; USRA 1918-1920; Nickel Plate purchase of the LE&W 1922 (lessor only); AC&Y - Northern Ohio merger 14 Jan 1944.
metadata.omitted: Not drawn, per the report's drawable fields: the Akron - Copley motor-car local of 1920 (its track is inside acy-akron-delphos); Mount Blanchard - Carey under the CD&StL, and the whole Delphos - Carey narrow gauge under the Eastern & Western Air Line and Cleveland & Western 1885-1890 (no passenger year sourced). Nothing toward Canton or Youngstown (never built).
metadata.freight_only_check: Every feature ends with its passenger service: the whole system was freight-only after 20 Jul 1951 (Feb 1952 Guide: 'Freight Service only'); Akron - Mogadore freight-only after the 1920 motor cars (no trains east of Akron in the Nov 1938 Guide); Goodyear, Brittain Yard and belt trackage excluded.
metadata.horsecar_check: None: steam throughout, with gasoline motor cars from 1920.

segments.note: The Northern Ohio Railway, leased to the Akron, Canton & Youngstown from 1 Mar 1920 (Akron - Copley Junction bought outright May 1920); the two companies merged 14 Jan 1944, which did not change who ran the trains. Aug 1920: mail, express and passengers hauled Akron - Delphos by the AC&Y's new gasoline cars on alternate days, the other train each way 'of the regular type' (Medina Sentinel). Jan and Apr 1921: the 'regular east bound train' (Medina Sentinel). Nov 1938 Official Guide: one round trip daily except Sunday, No. 95 Akron 10:30 AM - Delphos 6:15 PM, No. 90 Delphos 8:30 AM - Akron 4:30 PM, 25 stations, many flag stops; the same trains in a 1942 Akron listing. By March 1951 it was a mixed train, one passenger car on the rear of a freight, once each way daily; mail lost Oct 1950; the AC&Y petitioned the Ohio PUC to drop it (Bluffton News). Last run 20 Jul 1951 (Sanders 2007, via Wikipedia); the Feb 1952 Guide prints the table as 'Freight Service only'. Freight continued: Delphos - Carey to Dec 1982 (lifted 1984); Carey - Akron is the Wheeling & Lake Erie today. Headway is the 1938-1951 one train each way; 1920-21 had two each way. No source in hand confirms trains in 1922-1937 specifically, but the 1920, 1921, 1938, 1942 and 1951 anchors and the absence of any reported suspension support a continuous span.
sources: Segment-level: start (1 Mar 1920 lease; AC&Y passengers Aug 1920) from the Medina Sentinel and Wikipedia; service touched down 1921, 1938 (Official Guide with times), 1942 and Mar 1951; end (last run 20 Jul 1951) from Sanders 2007 via Wikipedia, corroborated by the Feb 1952 Guide.

segments.note: The Northern Ohio Railway (the reorganised Pittsburgh, Akron & Western, incorporated 10 Aug 1895), leased in perpetuity to and operated by the Lake Erie & Western from 1 Oct 1895 as its 'Northern Ohio Division'; trains were advertised under both names. Apr 1900 Akron directory: Northern Ohio depot North Main St, two trains each way. Jun 1902 Akron directory: 'Lake Erie & Western R.R. Northern Ohio Division', Nos. 1 and 11 out, 2 and 12 in, daily except Sunday, plus a Sunday excursion Akron - Delphos. Mar 1917: 'westbound Northern Ohio passenger train' delayed near Copley. Feb 1919: Northern Ohio and B&O passenger stations at Plymouth combined. NOT splits: New York Central stock control of the LE&W from Feb 1900; USRA federal control 1918 - 29 Feb 1920; the Nickel Plate's 1922 purchase of the LE&W (by then only the lessor). [OPEN] at both ends: 1900 and 1919 are the first and last CONFIRMED years, not known openings or endings. The LE&W ran the line from Oct 1895 to Feb 1920 and passengers almost certainly ran 1895-1899 and into 1920, but no source in hand proves it; 1919 rests on a passenger-station item, not a train (the last explicit train is 1917). Do not extend without evidence. Headway from the 1900/1902 two trains each way.
sources: Segment-level: 1900 and 1902 Akron Daily Democrat timetables with times; 1917 passenger train and 1919 passenger station, Medina Sentinel. Era dates (lease 1 Oct 1895, AC&Y lease 1 Mar 1920) from the AC&Y Historical Society and the Indianapolis Journal.
https://www.acyhs.org/ACY_Northern_Ohio_Railway.php (AC&Y Historical Society, Northern Ohio Ry history)

segments.note: Built 'by the people on its line': the Cleveland & Western narrow gauge Delphos - Carey standard-gauged 1890 and extended Carey - Akron 1890-91; trains west from Akron in early spring 1891, final Akron connection 28 May 1891. Apr 1891: line 'now completed and well equipped', general passenger agent issuing 500-mile tickets (Indianapolis Journal); passenger department moved to Akron Mar 1891. Receivership from 29 Jul 1893 and sale 17 Oct 1894 kept the same road and name — not a split. Jul 1894: excursion to Akron on the 'P. A. W.' (Wellington Enterprise). [OPEN] end: 1894 is the last CONFIRMED year, not a known ending; the PA&W era ran until the LE&W lease of 1 Oct 1895, but no 1895 passenger train is sourced. Do not extend without evidence. Whether Delphos - Carey carried PA&W passengers in 1890 is not established. Headway is an estimate (two trains each way, as under the LE&W in 1900), not sourced for this era.
sources: Segment-level: start from the Apr 1891 Indianapolis Journal (passenger tickets) and Mar 1891 Wellington Enterprise; end is the last confirmed year, a Jul 1894 excursion in the Wellington Enterprise. Headway NOT SOURCED (estimate).

segments.note: The AC&Y's own line (built Mogadore - Akron 1911-13). Aug 1920: the company's new gasoline cars 'have been in service for some time between Akron and Mogadore, and more recently as far west as Copley' (Medina Sentinel); together with the Akron - Copley run this was the Mogadore - Copley 'commuter service' (Grant 2010, via Wikipedia). The cars were 'discontinued in the fall' of 1920; a resumption to Copley was announced for 15 Apr 1921 but not confirmed. [ANCHOR]: 1920 is the one proven year. Wikipedia/Grant put the motor cars at 1920-1922, and service may have begun before 1920, but no other year is confirmed — do not widen without evidence. The Nov 1938 Guide shows no trains east of Akron; the line is freight-only (now Wheeling & Lake Erie). Headway is a guess, not sourced.
sources: Segment-level: 1920 motor-car service Akron - Mogadore from the Medina Sentinel 13 Aug 1920; discontinued fall 1920 per the Medina Sentinel 8 Apr 1921. Headway NOT SOURCED.

segments.note: 3 ft narrow gauge. 'Mixed trains began running the 17 miles between Delphos and Columbus Grove on January 25, 1882' (AC&Y Historical Society): two mixed trains each way daily at first, later cut to one. [ANCHOR]: 1882 is the only proven year. Service certainly ran wider — the CD&StL ran the line until its 1884 receivership and 1 Nov 1885 transfer to the Eastern & Western Air Line, and narrow-gauge trains ran under the Cleveland & Western until 1890 — but no other passenger year is confirmed in hand. Do not widen without evidence.
sources: Segment-level: AC&Y Historical Society CD&StL history (a society account with no primary citation).

segments.note: 3 ft narrow gauge via Pandora, Bluffton and Arlington. 'January 1, 1883, the road was formally opened by an excursion from Delphos to Mt Blanchard' (AC&Y Historical Society); the Bluffton News in 1951 independently dates Bluffton's passenger service from 1883. [ANCHOR]: 1883 is the one proven year (the opening excursion, a passenger special). Mixed trains very probably ran on through the 1880s, but no other year is confirmed — do not widen without evidence. Mount Blanchard - Carey (finished summer 1883) has no confirmed passenger year and is not drawn. Headway is a guess, not sourced.
